findings.finding: Resealed request/context could name another task while snapshot still named the selected task. Scope-only comparisons did not establish complete internal binding.
findings.resolution: Task-directory, task/repository/requester/phase/parameters/artifact/policy/time bindings are reconstructed from snapshot; recorded policy output is replayed. Coherent wrong-task and decision-forgery cases now reject.

findings.finding: Governance escalate and evaluator inconclusive produced observed/complete/ok=true without exposing verdicts.
findings.resolution: Explicit verdict fields and needs_followup keep unresolved negative reviews pending/ok=false. Accepted technical review of a correctly handled denial remains possible without action authority.

findings.finding: Freshness omitted relevant launcher/schema/dependency inputs and selected-root equality was not enforced.
findings.resolution: Implementation/schema/requirements/runtime identities enter the fingerprint; both launcher and worker reject a different registered checkout even with the same UUID. Tests cover schema/launcher drift and clone mismatch.

findings.finding: A success-shaped child summary with null record/snapshot/decision could be accepted.
findings.resolution: Observed/review_pending states require nonnull well-formed bindings and consistent status/ok/review verdict combinations. Malformed child output is rejected without raw echo.

findings.finding: Oversized valid-looking identifiers were accepted and echoed in error metadata beyond the128-character contract.
findings.resolution: Identifier length is capped before filesystem/child access; task/repository/selector boundary tests verify bounded sanitized errors.

findings.finding: Abrupt termination or contention could leave a persistent lock with only a generic failure and unclear safe recovery.
findings.resolution: observation_locked is explicit; no automatic deletion. Documented recovery requires confirmed process exit and exact unchanged lock identity; tests preserve all records and verify retry after simulated externally verified recovery.

findings.finding: Unconditional optional-module import broke copied no-config legacy runtimes.
findings.resolution: All three hook sites use one profile-presence guard. No profile skips the import; configured missing module reports sanitized advisory unavailable. Legacy CLI and lifecycle tests pass.

findings.finding: Publication worktree hashes and git diff cleanliness could misrepresent committed contents under assume-unchanged or CRLF conversion.
findings.resolution: Publication binds the sole actual commit parent/base and exact full changed/staged set. NUL-delimited ls-tree metadata supplies mode/type/OID/size and explicit deletions, including managed files. content_basis distinguishes git-object-metadata from working-tree-bytes. No blob or working-file contents are read for publication metadata.

findings.finding: Intermediate/invalid cached records needed an explicit recoverable path without hiding corruption or carrying old reviews forward.
findings.resolution: observe --refresh preserves old bytes and bounded prior-ID/digest/validation references, reruns all normal prepare/policy/consistency checks, and creates an unreviewed record. Oversized prior data has no invented full digest; invalid index/linked paths are not repaired.

live_assessment.meaning: Accepted for the inspected P0 implementation and workspace observation, not execution permission or approval of a later commit. This assessment is historical after its expiry or relevant snapshot change.

environment_observations: The initial no-config copied-runtime failure was a genuine compatibility defect and was fixed, not dismissed as environment noise.

The initial force-terminated context-lock case failed under the observer venv. The existing context suite passed under its actual configured bundled hook interpreter; the failed venv log remains retained. The venv scenario is not falsely reported as passed.

A bounded evaluator-owned sleep-only child diagnostic did not reproduce orphaning: launcher and Python worker PIDs differed but the worker terminated after launcher kill. No user process was touched and this did not establish a universal process-tree guarantee.
limitations: This is selected lifecycle observation, not interception or enforcement of every agent tool call. Existing independently authorized publication can proceed when observation is unavailable.
Records are append-only through this API and self-consistency checked, but local writable files and declared reviewer identities are not authenticated audit evidence or grants.
Workspace fingerprints and checked path components do not provide an atomic filesystem snapshot or OS security boundary against a concurrent privileged writer.
Publication content identity is immutable Git object metadata; it does not scan blob content, authenticate permission, or imply the current worktree equals the committed bytes.
Actual same-checkout development selection and HTTPS publication metadata are the bounded rollout. Other environments/services/checkouts are not silently enabled.
Protected execution, trusted identity/signing, credential/network isolation, P1 gates, operational continuous AI assurance and legal compliance remain not_run/outside this P0 task.

Final result submission, task-owned commit/push and remote confirmation belong to the main session. A later publication observation is separate from the reviewed workspace record and must not inherit this assessment as authority.
